title: On with plural owners
focus: Use fixed on with meillä, teillä, and heillä to say what the owner has.

exercises.prompt: Choose “You have a book.” in Finnish. Use teillä (“you as the owner”) and kirja (“a book”). Frame: “Teillä ___ kirja”. Address a group.
exercises.explanation: Possession uses on with every owner. Plural owners still take on; ovat belongs to a different sentence pattern.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Fixed on in possession: form or meaning confused

Possession uses on with every owner. Plural owners still take on; ovat belongs to a different sentence pattern.

This choice changes the required polarity or leaves the required question pattern.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed on + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: te has the learned possession form teillä; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Olla means “to be”; possession uses its fixed on form with every owner, including we and they.
kirja stays in its basic singular form: one book.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed on in possession: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
